problem_checks.analysis: Definition p2 includes the identity group and the complete theorem omits nontriviality. On Gm every Ga action fixes the Laurent unit because units of C[s,z,z^-1] are c*z^m, with s0 identity forcing c1,m1. Thus identity is maximal unipotent but not maximal commutative. A1,U1 also defeats the universal centralizer claim. Claim1 p9 explicitly chooses nonzero u; corrected nontrivial theorem and Cor5.3 retain their stated separate assumptions. This is a false central classification case, not a general reconstruction counterexample.

The Ga4 action (a,b).(x,t)=(x+ta+b,t) is faithful; quotient/fibres, smooth affine product, complementary Uprime and irreducible stabilizer fibres all meet p9. E={ta=0} has a maximal vertical dimension2 component and a horizontal dimension1 component. Dominance asserted for a maximal component fails. Injectivity of the infinitesimal action is open; characteristic0 removes finite vector subgroups, and the fibre argument gives the free translation model. This is a replacement for a false centralizer-proof inference used in TheoremA, not a theorem counterexample.

Definition p6 makes ordinary roots dimension1; p18 includes arbitrary-dimensional generalized roots. Scalar dilation of A2 with two-dimensional translations under identity is admissible. The actual p19 proof establishes algebraicity and dimension, and pairwise diagonal lines force a common scalar character. The corrected generalized conclusion matches later use; the terminology mismatch is local.

Source pp14-15 chooses Z^m outside forbidden affine sublattices and then asserts a regular monomial. In H=Ga_x x Gm_y on A2, a=-1 is allowed but y^-1 gives a nonregular rational replica. The required regular-root construction is actually used p23 for Di,Tj simultaneously, then Lemma7.5 unifies the field automorphism in Theorem8.5(a), Theorem9.1/C. Choosing N^m outside a finite union of proper affine linear zero sets is valid by polynomial induction and repairs this core step. Separate rank=m-1 overstatement fails for T1=T2=Gm2, but rank<=m-1 suffices and remains Minor.

Gm x mu2 as a closed diagonalizable group on A2 has dimension1 and 2-torsion rank2, satisfying p20. A prime not dividing the finite component-group order has the claimed rank, which already suffices for the dimension inequality. The failure is exceptional-prime quantification, not the dimension conclusion.

Theorem8.5 p22 requires source non-torus and H<=G. The p25 toric application uses H=DGa not inside torus G, and p27 starts from a torus. Their exact examples meet the surrounding construction. The p25 algebraicity already established allows corrected Prop8.1(a) both ways; trivial-weight roots lie in self-centralizing D x Ga. The p27 replacement Cor5.3 inverse plus Lemma3.4 is already the route in Remark9.2 p26. These are local mis-invocations with required ingredients available, not broader counterexamples.

Theorem10.1 p27 without an n restriction is false for n1,Gamma1,point Z. Its actual finite-kernel branch has n>=3: n1 excludes 0<r<n, and n2 maps an infinite group to finite GL1Z. No counterexample to that actual use, nor a reproof of external Cantat-Xie/Margulis, is claimed.

Actual p11 image and text distinguish precomposition closed immersion End(X)->Mor(W,X) from postcomposition mere morphism End(W)->Mor(W,X). The source proceeds by locally closed orbit and subgroup arguments. The original allegation and its family z->az test a statement absent from the source. Withdrawn, with the original report/evidence preserved as historical.
